source.author: verg
source.text: Nos abiisse rati et vento petiisse Mycenas:
source.text_original: Nos abiisse rati et vento petiisse Mycenas: /
source.text_english: We thought that we had departed and had been driven by the wind to Mycenae:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: quin etiam Herculeo consurgit ab ordine Tydeus Nelidesque Periclymenus, quem parva Methone felevis Elis equis et fluctibus obvius Aulon caestibus adversos viderunt frangere vultus. Tu quoque Phrixeos remo, Poeantie, Colchos bis Lemnon visure petis, nunc cuspide patris inclitus, Herculeas olim moture sagittas.
reuse.text_original: quin etiam Herculeo consurgit ab ordine Tydeus / Nelidesque Periclymenus, quem parva Methone / †felevis Elis equis et fluctibus obvius Aulon / caestibus adversos viderunt frangere vultus. — / Tu quoque Phrixeos remo, Poeantie, Colchos / bis Lemnon visure petis, nunc cuspide patris / inclitus, Herculeas olim moture sagittas.
reuse.text_english: Indeed, too, Tydeus rises from the Heraclean line, and the son of Neleus, Periclymenus, whom small Methone, Elis famed for its horses, and Aulon, facing the waves, saw breaking the faces of their opponents with fists. You too, Poeantius, seek Phrixian Colchis by oar, about to see Lemnos twice, now renowned for your father’s spear, once destined to wield Heraclean arrows.
